correctness.rationale: The matrix determinant lemma reduces each fiber to a linear coefficient map. For fixed u its kernel is the annihilator of the cyclic Krylov subspace and its image is exactly (chi_A/g_u) times the polynomials below degree deg(g_u); both assertions are established by triangular polynomial division. Primary kernel sizes count the u-exponents exactly; multiplication yields the target formula. Removing the zero-update factorizations and applying strict partition dominance proves the remaining claims. Literal determinant enumeration verifies complete target fibers for 10 canonical types and 92 targets; finite tests are supplementary.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2023 theorem dominates all existence claims here, so those are explicitly not claimed new. The classical fixed-input pole assignment claim is also covered; it does not supply multiplicities after summation over all possible input vectors.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Bounds and existence do not determine fiber multiplicity. The older resolvent identity implies the starting linear algebra reduction but not, without the new exact cyclic-annihilator enumeration, the product of primary-partition differences or its strict monotonicity. A hidden equivalent counting theorem remains possible. The novelty assessment expressly excludes the fixed-u portion and hinges on the complete all-u primary-partition formula and strict dominance.

value.rationale: The full finite-field target-by-target characteristic-polynomial distribution for arbitrary fixed base matrices is a motivated invariant beyond reachability. It distinguishes primary similarity types with identical characteristic polynomial by a strict Jordan-dominance law, and yields sharply contrasting uniform irreducible and concentrated scalar regimes. These are complete natural classifications usable for finite-field spectral perturbations.
